opennyai_summary.facts: This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 9.5.1997 passed by Special Judge S.C. Act/Addl. Sessions Judge, Etawah convicting the revisionist under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentencing him to one year rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 2000/- and in default of payment of fine further R.I. for six months.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended by learned counsel for revisionist that revisionist was entitled for release by giving benefit of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1958") but Trial Court without considering this fact that applicant is first offender, convicted the applicant sentencing him to one year rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of 2,000/-.
It is next contended that in the Ajai Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 20 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128605750/
1 present matter, Trial Court neither invoked the "Act, 1958" nor provision of Section 360 Cr.P.C. by sentencing the accused-revisionist.
In support of his contention, he has placed reliance upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Dhurukumar s/o Radhakishan Pitti and another vs. State of Maharashtra as well as order of this Court dated 15.5.2019 in Criminal Appeal No.745 of 2007 (Durgesh Chandra Vs. State of U.P.).
The accused-revisionist has no criminal antecedents.
Learned A.G.A. has submitted that he has no objection and further submitted that accused-revisionist is not a previous convict.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this revision deserves to be allowed in part on the point of sentence.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
The conviction of accused-revisionist recorded by Court below is hereby affirmed and upheld.
The quantum of sentence is being modified.
Revisionist be released giving benefit of Section 4 of Act, 1958 on execution of personal bond of Rs.20,000/- with photograph on the condition of maintaining peace and good behaviour for a period of two years from the date of acceptance of bond by the concerned Court below.
The personal bond shall be filed to the satisfaction of concerned Court below.
In the event of breach of aforesaid conditions, the Court below would be competent to summon the accused and would be at liberty to pass appropriate orders for sentence against accused-revisionist in accordance with law, keeping in view the judgment of Lower Appellate Court.
With the aforesaid observations, this revision is partly allowed and judgment and order dated 9.5.1997 passed by Lower Appellate Court is modified accordingly.
Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
